title: Ultrasonic: seeing with sound
about: How a robot measures distance with echoes, and what can fool it.

html: An ultrasonic sensor finds things the way a bat does: it chirps, then listens for the echo.

<text x="250" y="22" fill="#f4f1ea" font-size="15" font-weight="700">MICROPHONE</text><text x="250" y="40" fill="#aaa6b0" font-size="12">hears the echo</text></g>

The chirp vibrates 40,000 times per second. People can only hear up to about 20,000, so it's too high for us. That's why it's called ultrasonic: beyond sound.
Time the echo
The sensor starts a timer when it chirps and stops it when the echo comes back. Sound travels about 343 meters per second, and it goes there and back, so:
distance = 343 × time ÷ 2
The times are tiny, so we use milliseconds (ms), thousandths of a second. An echo after 10 ms means 343 × 0.010 ÷ 2 ≈ 1.7 m.
The chirp spreads out in a cone, like a flashlight beam. The sensor reports the closest thing inside the cone.
Why some things fool it
• Soft things like pillows, couches, and curtains soak up sound instead of bouncing it back.
• Tilted walls can bounce the sound off to the side, like a ball hitting a wall at an angle. Then the echo never reaches the microphone.
• Far things: sound gets weaker as it spreads out. A typical classroom sensor can't hear echoes from more than about 4 m away.
Every time, the robot hears nothing and thinks the path is clear. That's how robots crash!

steps.q: The echo comes back after 6 ms (0.006 seconds). About how far away is the wall?
steps.explain: 343 × 0.006 = 2.06 m there and back. Divide by 2: about 1.0 m.

steps.q: Why did the tilted wall fool the sensor?
options: Tilted walls are always too far away
The echo bounced off to the side and never came back
The wall soaked up the sound
steps.explain: Sound bounces like a ball. Off a tilted wall it goes sideways, so the microphone never hears it.

steps.q: In Bot Arena, what does the Ultrasonic sensor help your robot do best?
steps.explain: It measures distance, so your robot dodges better. Its aim is okay, but the Camera aims best.
